author: nc1234
content: what's the "it" in your message? Not sure if you are referring to the IL roots or the bit list. I believe having IL roots in the bid is what makes builders accountable. With the bit list, a set bit doesn't say which IL the builder meant, so when a ILC member equivocates you can't tell a lying builder from an honest one that saw the other IL. With the root in the bid, the claim is specific and you can check the payload against that exact IL.

author: nc1234
content:
Say ILC member 5 equivocates and publishes IL A and IL B. Builder sets bit 5 and its payload includes A's txs. I only saw B, so to me the payload claims bit 5 and fails bit 5. I have no way to tell whether the builder lied or just saw A. Either I blacklist an honest builder or I let the liar go. 
If the bid carried A's root instead of bit 5, I would see a root I don't hold, fetch it, and find a signed IL from member 5. That tells me member 5 equivocated and the builder was honest. And a liar that named A's root can't escape, because the claim is pinned to that exact IL and a later IL B doesn't change what A's root refers to.
